question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the secant-tangent identity 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic secant-tangent identity

$$
1-{tanh}^{2}⁡x={sech}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we rewrite the integral and evaluate it, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}({coth}^{2}⁡x-{coth}^{2}⁡x{tanh}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}{coth}^{2}⁡x\cdot (1-{tanh}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}{coth}^{2}⁡x\cdot {sech}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\frac{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\cdot \frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\frac{1}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}{csch}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{coth}⁡x{|}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\  & =-(\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡4)-\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)) \\  & =\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)-\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡4) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡2}}{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡2}}-\frac{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡4}}{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}-{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡4}} \\  & =\frac{2+{2}^{-1}}{2-{2}^{-1}}-\frac{4+{4}^{-1}}{4-{4}^{-1}} \\  & =\frac{5}{3}-\frac{17}{15} \\  & =\frac{8}{15}\end{aligned}
$$
